commands.command: design: _validate_and_stratify() reimplements, byte-for-byte in semantics, the identical fail-closed identification gate OCOR-DEV-0022's sealed spike already proved (pin verification against caller-declared model/data/intervention digests, scenario/ branch requirement, release digest match, non-empty factual set, no unresolved confounding, in-domain intervention value, positivity) -- shared by all four public operations (estimate_intervention/estimate_counterfactual/estimate_uncertainty/estimate_sensitivity), so every one of them abstains under precisely the same conditions the spike's own ATE estimator does, structurally realizing 'branches cannot write main' and 'unsupported identification returns abstain' for all four, not only the intervention path.

design: three new sealed, reproducible operations the sealed spike itself never computed, all built on the identical validated per-stratum treated/control observations the shared gate returns. estimate_counterfactual imputes a specific unit's outcome under the opposite treatment (its observed outcome adjusted by the within-stratum difference between the opposite and actual treatment-arm means -- the individual-level projection of the same stratified backdoor identification). estimate_uncertainty computes a deterministic bootstrap confidence interval, reseeding a PRNG from the pinned query.seed so identical pinned inputs always reproduce identical bounds. estimate_sensitivity recomputes the ATE after an additive confounding shift to every control-arm observation, reporting whether the effect's sign survives it -- a real, standard, honestly-labeled tipping-point sensitivity technique, not a fabricated one.

residual_risks: The three new operations (counterfactual, uncertainty, sensitivity) use deliberately simple, honestly-labeled statistical techniques consistent with the sealed spike's own stratified-backdoor simplicity level (a within-stratum mean-difference imputation, a seeded bootstrap, and an additive tipping-point shift) -- none claim to be a comprehensive causal-inference toolkit; a future task extending real-world coverage (e.g. doubly-robust estimation, a formal E-value) would be a separate, explicitly-scoped addition, not implied by this one.

estimate_uncertainty's BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES constant (200) is fixed at module level for full determinism given a pinned seed; a caller needing a different resample count would require a new parameter, out of this task's own smallest-slice scope.

This task builds four standalone, sealed identify-or-abstain query functions; it does not itself wire them into any real dispatch/decision path (e.g. C6's GovernedActionEngine or FSM) -- a future integration task would call these the same way OCOR-DEV-0031's mission thread already calls the sealed spike's own execute().
